finding: Database Pulse advances to a two-phase V5 lifecycle: cognition reads do not mutate physical schema; build/drop maintenance is planned and executed between Pulses against exact epoch/hash basis, model output remains quarantined/no-authority, and physical maintenance now has CAS-atomic durable receipts. This is a stronger Frank runtime candidate, not release proof.
negative_evidence: V4 could create an index inside select() and leave it maintained after controller switched ONLINE; V5 exists to remove this lifecycle/resource defect.
Cheap authenticated-shadow refresh is not a global tamper oracle; focused-row verification plus periodic/full audit remains required.
counterhypotheses: The added Pulse/index lifecycle machinery may cost more than always-online queries under high churn or short reuse horizons.
Equivalent behavior may be achievable with a simpler evented scheduler plus conventional indexed SQLite without a distinct Pulse rank subsystem.
boundaries: Database Pulse is endogenous Frank state/cognition runtime, not the LLM inference loop.
Hostinger/GitHub Ubuntu evidence is preliminary and cannot satisfy final target acceptance.
Frank v0.1 final acceptance remains Andreas Ubuntu only.
ancestry_policy: V3/V4/V5, their tests, workflows and benchmark descendants share implementation/supervisor ancestry and are not independent replications.
